{{DISPLAYTITLE:''q''-Gaussian process}}
'''q-Gaussian processes''' are deformations of the usual [[Gaussian distribution]]. There are several different versions of this; here we treat a multivariate deformation, also addressed as q-Gaussian process, arising from [[free probability theory]] and corresponding to deformations of the [[canonical commutation relations]]. For other deformations of Gaussian distributions, see [[q-Gaussian distribution]] and [[Gaussian q-distribution]].

== History ==

The q-Gaussian process was formally introduced in a paper by Frisch and Bourret<ref name=FB1970>{{cite journal |last1=Frisch |first1=U. |last2=Bourret |first2=R. |title=Parastochastics |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |date=February 1970 |volume=11 |issue=2 |pages=364–390 |doi=10.1063/1.1665149 |bibcode=1970JMP....11..364F }}</ref> under the name of ''parastochastics'', and also later by Greenberg<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Greenberg |first1=O. W. |title=Example of infinite statistics |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=12 February 1990 |volume=64 |issue=7 |pages=705–708 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.64.705 |pmid=10042057 |bibcode=1990PhRvL..64..705G }}</ref> as an example of ''infinite statistics''. It was mathematically established and investigated in
papers by Bozejko and Speicher<ref name=BS1991>{{cite journal |last1=Bożejko |first1=Marek |last2=Speicher |first2=Roland |title=An example of a generalized Brownian motion |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=April 1991 |volume=137 |issue=3 |pages=519–531 |doi=10.1007/BF02100275 |bibcode=1991CMaPh.137..519B |s2cid=123190397 |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104202738 }}</ref> and by Bozejko, Kümmerer, and Speicher<ref name=BKS1997>{{cite journal |last1=Bożejko |first1=M. |last2=Kümmerer |first2=B. |last3=Speicher |first3=R. |title=q-Gaussian Processes: Non-commutative and Classical Aspects |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=1 April 1997 |volume=185 |issue=1 |pages=129–154 |doi=10.1007/s002200050084 |arxiv=funct-an/9604010 |bibcode=1997CMaPh.185..129B |s2cid=2993071 }}</ref> in the context of non-commutative probability.

It is given as the distribution of sums of creation and annihilation operators in a q-deformed [[Fock space]]. The calculation of moments of those operators is given by a q-deformed version of a [[Wick theorem|Wick formula]] or [[Isserlis' theorem|Isserlis formula]]. The specification of a special covariance in the underlying [[Hilbert space]] leads to the [[q-Brownian motion]],<ref name=BKS1997 /> a special non-commutative version of classical [[Brownian motion]].

== q-Fock space ==

In the following <math> q\in[-1,1] </math> is fixed.
Consider a Hilbert space <math> \mathcal{H} </math>. On the algebraic full Fock space
: <math>
  \mathcal{F}_\text{alg}(\mathcal{H})=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{H}^{\otimes n},
</math>
where <math>\mathcal{H}^0=\mathbb{C}\Omega</math> with a norm one vector <math>\Omega</math>, called ''vacuum'', we define a q-deformed inner product as follows:

:<math>
   \langle h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n,g_1\otimes\cdots\otimes g_m\rangle_q = \delta_{nm}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod^n_{r=1}\langle h_r,g_{\sigma(r)}\rangle q^{i(\sigma)},
</math>

where <math>i(\sigma)=\#\{(k,\ell)\mid 1\leq k<\ell\leq n; \sigma(k)>\sigma(\ell)\}</math> is the number of inversions of <math>\sigma\in S_n</math>.

The ''q-Fock space''<ref name=EP03>{{cite journal |last1=Effros |first1=Edward G. |last2=Popa |first2=Mihai |title=Feynman diagrams and Wick products associated with q-Fock space |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=22 July 2003 |volume=100 |issue=15 |pages=8629–8633 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1531460100 |pmid=12857947 |pmc=166362 |arxiv=math/0303045 |bibcode=2003PNAS..100.8629E |doi-access=free }}</ref> is then defined as the completion of the algebraic full Fock space with respect to this inner product
:<math>
 \mathcal{F}_q(\mathcal{H})=\overline{\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{H}^{\otimes n}}^{\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_q}.
</math>
For <math> -1 < q < 1 </math> the q-inner product is strictly positive.<ref name=BS1991 /><ref name=Z1992>{{cite journal |last1=Zagier |first1=Don |title=Realizability of a model in infinite statistics |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=June 1992 |volume=147 |issue=1 |pages=199–210 |doi=10.1007/BF02099535 |bibcode=1992CMaPh.147..199Z |s2cid=53385666 }}</ref> For <math> q=1</math> and <math> q=-1 </math> it is positive, but has a kernel, which leads in these cases to the symmetric and anti-symmetric Fock spaces, respectively.

For <math>h\in\mathcal{H}</math> we define the ''q-creation operator'' <math>a^*(h)</math>, given by
:<math>
 a^*(h)\Omega=h,\qquad
  a^*(h)h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n=h\otimes h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n.
</math>
Its adjoint (with respect to the q-inner product), the ''q-annihilation operator'' <math>a(h)</math>, is given by
:<math>
  a(h)\Omega=0,\qquad
  a(h)h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n=\sum_{r=1}^n q^{r-1} \langle h,h_r\rangle h_1\otimes \cdots \otimes h_{r-1}\otimes h_{r+1}\otimes\cdots \otimes h_n.
</math>

== q-commutation relations ==

Those operators satisfy the q-commutation relations<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kennedy |first1=Matthew |last2=Nica |first2=Alexandru |title=Exactness of the Fock Space Representation of the q-Commutation Relations |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=9 September 2011 |volume=308 |issue=1 |pages=115–132 |doi=10.1007/s00220-011-1323-9 |arxiv=1009.0508 |bibcode=2011CMaPh.308..115K |s2cid=119124507 }}</ref>
:<math>a(f)a^*(g)-q a^*(g)a(f)=\langle f,g\rangle \cdot 1\qquad (f,g\in \mathcal{H}).</math>
For <math> q=1 </math>, <math> q=0 </math>, and <math> q=-1 </math> this reduces to the CCR-relations, the Cuntz relations, and the CAR-relations, respectively. With the exception of the case <math>q=1,</math> the operators <math>a^*(f)</math> are bounded.

== q-Gaussian elements and definition of multivariate q-Gaussian distribution (q-Gaussian process) ==

Operators of the form <math> s_q(h)={a(h)+a^*(h)}
</math>
for <math>h\in\mathcal{H}</math> are called ''q-Gaussian''<ref name=EP03 /> (or ''q-semicircular''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Vergès |first1=Matthieu Josuat |title=Cumulants of the q-semicircular Law, Tutte Polynomials, and Heaps |journal=Canadian Journal of Mathematics |date=20 November 2018 |volume=65 |issue=4 |pages=863–878 |doi=10.4153/CJM-2012-042-9 |arxiv=1203.3157 |s2cid=2215028 }}</ref>) elements.

On <math>\mathcal{F}_q(\mathcal{H})</math> we consider the ''vacuum expectation state''
<math> \tau(T)=\langle \Omega,T\Omega \rangle</math>, for <math>T\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{H}))</math>.

The ''(multivariate) q-Gaussian distribution'' or ''q-Gaussian process''<ref name=BKS1997/><ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Bryc | first1 = Włodzimierz
 | last2 = Wang | first2 = Yizao
 | arxiv = 1511.06667
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Probability and Mathematical Statistics
 | mr = 3593028
 | pages = 335–352
 | title = The local structure of {{mvar|q}}-Gaussian processes
 | volume = 36
 | year = 2016}}</ref> is defined as the non commutative distribution of a collection of q-Gaussians with respect to the vacuum expectation state. For <math>h_1,\dots,h_p\in\mathcal{H}</math> the joint distribution of <math>s_q(h_1),\dots,s_q(h_p)</math> with respect to <math>\tau</math> can be described in the following way,:<ref name=FB1970 /><ref name=BS1991 /> for any <math>i\{1,\dots,k\}\rightarrow\{1,\dots,p\}</math> we have
:<math>
 \tau\left(s_q(h_{i(1)})\cdots s_q(h_{i(k)})\right)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{P}_2(k)} q^{cr(\pi)} \prod_{(r,s)\in\pi} \langle h_{i(r)}, h_{i(s)} \rangle,
</math>
where <math>cr(\pi)</math> denotes the number of crossings of the pair-partition <math>\pi</math>. This is a q-deformed version of the Wick/Isserlis formula.

== q-Gaussian distribution in the one-dimensional case ==

For ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1, the q-Gaussian distribution is a probability measure on the interval <math>[-2/\sqrt{1-q}, 2/\sqrt{1-q}]</math>, with analytic formulas for its density.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Leeuwen |first1=Hans van |last2=Maassen |first2=Hans |title=A ''q'' deformation of the Gauss distribution |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |date=September 1995 |volume=36 |issue=9 |pages=4743–4756 |doi=10.1063/1.530917 |bibcode=1995JMP....36.4743V |hdl=2066/141604 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> For the special cases <math> q=1 </math>, <math> q=0 </math>, and <math> q=-1 </math>, this reduces to the classical Gaussian distribution, the [[Wigner semicircle distribution]], and the symmetric [[Bernoulli distribution]] on <math>\pm 1</math>. The determination of the density follows from old results<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szegö |first1=G |title=Ein Beitrag zur Theorie der Thetafunktionen |trans-title=A contribution to the theory of theta functions |language=German |journal=Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Phys.-Math. Klasse |pages=242–252 |year=1926 }}</ref> on corresponding [[orthogonal polynomials]].

== Operator algebraic questions ==

The [[von Neumann algebra]] generated by <math> s_q(h_i) </math>, for <math> h_i </math> running through an orthonormal system <math> (h_i)_{i\in I} </math> of vectors in <math> \mathcal{H} </math>, reduces for <math> q=0 </math> to the famous free group factors <math> L(F_{\vert I\vert}) </math>. Understanding the structure of those von Neumann algebras for general q has been a source of many investigations.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Wasilewski | first = Mateusz
 | arxiv = 1907.00730
 | doi = 10.4064/cm7968-11-2019
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Colloquium Mathematicum
 | mr = 4162298
 | pages = 1–14
 | title = A simple proof of the complete metric approximation property for {{mvar|q}}-Gaussian algebras
 | volume = 163
 | year = 2021}}</ref> It is now known, by work of Guionnet and Shlyakhtenko,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Guionnet |first1=A. |last2=Shlyakhtenko |first2=D. |title=Free monotone transport |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |date=13 November 2013 |volume=197 |issue=3 |pages=613–661 |doi=10.1007/s00222-013-0493-9 |arxiv=1204.2182 |s2cid=16882208 }}</ref> that at least for finite I and for small values of q, the von Neumann algebra is isomorphic to the corresponding free group factor.
